results.resolution: Companion to r13 (apply r13 first or together): access permit/rules/closures/land manager/parking/overnight permit, emergency notes/county/dispatch/ranger station/hospital, best_season, seasonal_guidance window and July/August reasons, climate summer/typical/forecastZone and comms re-pointed from Stehekin/Agnes Creek to the Cascade Pass trailhead and Ptarmigan Traverse line. access.fees and access._raw untouched.
results.summary: After r13, the access, emergency, season, climate and comms fields still sent climbers to Stehekin; this rewrites them for the Cascade Pass / Ptarmigan Traverse approach.
results.evidence: Eighth pass, 2026-10-01. Land/county by coordinate: USFS EDW boundary services put Cache Col and Kool-Aid Lake in the Glacier Peak Wilderness, Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie NF (Mt. Baker RD), and Rimrock Ridge (GNIS 48.37557,-120.97826) and Yang Yang Lakes in the Glacier Peak Wilderness, Okanogan-Wenatchee NF (Chelan RD); the trailhead returns no forest (park land). Census geocoder: trailhead, Cache Col, Kool-Aid Skagit; Yang Yang and Rimrock Chelan. GNIS lists Cache Col, Cascade Pass, Sentinel and Le Conte on both counties (the crest is the line). Closures: NPS fire-closure list and the OWNF Sisi order (trails-only) both close Agnes Creek-side trails and neither names Cascade River Road or the Cascade Pass trail; NPS road page shows Cascade River Road OPEN, paved to about mile 10. Permits: NPS and WTA agree permits for Cascade River Road camps are picked up in person at the Marblemount WIC; SummitPost (2011 addition, after asking Marblemount rangers) and rocknropenw agree Cache Col is the park boundary and no park permit is needed beyond it. SummitPost's older body text says a backcountry permit is needed 'along the traverse' - superseded by its own 2011 addition and by rocknropenw. Parking: NPS fees page, WTA, SummitPost, 10adventures: no pass at a trailhead on park land (rocknropenw's NW Forest Pass is for the two-car through-trip). Hospital: PeaceHealth fact sheet + WA DOH snapshot both list Marblemount in United General's service area; 'nearest' not claimed. NOT WRITTEN: access.fees (open product decision) - it would need its ferry fare and High Bridge shuttle sentence removed and its park-fee clause scoped to camps inside the park (NPS + WTA: $10 per person plus $6 reservation fee; earthtrekkers quotes $26 per trip, so the per-night wording should be checked); the 'Forest Service wilderness permit beyond the park boundary is free' clause has no second source for this side. access.group_limit (12) left: SummitPost gives a six-person party limit for the traverse, one source, unverified for 2026. Not in scope but noticed: crowds.peakTraffic and seasonal_hazards.weather say 'Late July-September' / generic (compatible); bivy, road, approach, hazards etc. are r13's. Session owner: access.fees keeps its scoped park-fee sentences; only the Stehekin ferry / High Bridge shuttle sentence is removed, since the row no longer uses that approach (single-row edit, not a sweep).

ops.expect: An NPS wilderness permit is required for any overnight camping within the park/NRA boundary near High Bridge (reserve on recreation.gov or get a walk-up permit at the Golden West Visitor Center in Stehekin). Once across into the Glacier Peak Wilderness (Forest Service land), only a free self-issue wilderness permit is required, available at trailhead registration boxes.
ops.value: A North Cascades National Park wilderness permit is needed for any overnight stay inside the park, which on this approach is the ground from the Cascade Pass trailhead up to Cache Col. Permits for camps reached from the Cascade River Road are picked up in person at the Wilderness Information Center in Marblemount. Cache Col is the park boundary: beyond it the traverse is in the Glacier Peak Wilderness, where no park permit is needed to camp, and the usual first camp, Kool-Aid Lake, is already past it.

ops.expect: Leave No Trace travel required; camping is restricted to designated/permitted sites within the park/NRA portion of the approach. Food storage from bears is essential — aggressive bear activity has been reported in 2026 at PCT camps in this corridor (Fireweed and South Fork camps in particular).
ops.value: Inside the park, camping is allowed only at designated camps, and none is allowed at Cascade Pass itself or along the Cascade Pass trail; fires are not allowed at the backcountry camps there. Leave No Trace travel throughout.

ops.expect: As of mid-2026 the Stehekin area is still recovering from a historic December 2025 flood: Company Creek Road lost roughly 1,000 ft of roadbed and a levee (an elevated interim road was completed June 23, 2026); North Cascades Lodge at Stehekin is closed for the season (no lodging, dining, fuel, or showers, though ferry and postal service continue); the High Bridge shuttle bus is not running for 2026. On the trail itself, the Agnes Creek bridge at Hemlock Camp (south of the park boundary, in the Glacier Peak Wilderness) is out of service and camping at Hemlock Camp is considered unsafe due to hazard trees — use Cedar Camp or the South Fork Agnes Creek camp instead. Confirm current conditions with the Wilderness Information Center (360-854-7245) before going. Sisi Fire: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest closure order 06-17-02-2026-35 (Sisi Fire), in effect August 22 through December 31, 2026 unless lifted sooner, closes the Pacific Crest Trail (Trail 2000) along Agnes Creek on the Chelan Ranger District, along with Agnes Creek Trail 1272, Agnes Gorge Trail 1281 and Swamp Creek Trail 1242. North Cascades National Park's Sisi Fire closures (its fire-closure list, updated September 14, 2026, gives no end date) also close the Pacific Crest Trail from the park boundary down to High Bridge and on to Bridge Creek Camp, the High Bridge area, and the Stehekin Valley Road from Stehekin Valley Ranch to High Bridge. This approach cannot be used while these closures stand. Chelan Ranger District: (509) 682-4900. North Cascades National Park: (360) 854-7200.
ops.value: The Sisi Fire closures are on the Agnes Creek side of the ridge, not on this approach: they shut the Pacific Crest Trail along Agnes Creek and the Agnes Gorge trail, among others, so none of those valleys is a way out from the ridge while the closures stand. Neither the national forest's closure order nor the park's fire-closure list includes the Cascade River Road or the Cascade Pass trail.

ops.expect: Typically late July through September, once the approach brushfields and any lingering snow on the ridge have melted out. Earlier in the season expect mosquitoes in the lower Agnes Creek valley and possible snow on north-facing sections of the ridge. Check current NPS/USFS trail-condition reports before going, since bridges and camps in this corridor were still being repaired in 2026 after the December 2025 Stehekin flood.
ops.value: Usually from mid-July through August, and into September. Early in the season more snow lies on the glaciers and on the exposed ledge crossings, which makes the ledges harder; later in the summer the glaciers show more bare ice, the Le Conte Glacier above all.

ops.expect: Dry east-Cascades climate in the rain shadow of the crest — hot summer days, cool nights, and a much shorter, drier snow season than the west-side Cascades. Afternoon thunderstorms are common in July and August.
ops.value: The approach follows the Cascade crest, which divides the wetter, cloudier west side from the drier, warmer east side; the ridge itself lies on the east side. Storms can bring days of rain and wind even in summer, so allow a spare day for weather.
